headline: MV June Aster Death Toll Rises to 35 After Rescuers Enter Burned Ferry
seoTitle: MV June Aster Ferry Fire Death Toll Rises to 35 | FMB News
seoDescription: The death toll in the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron rose to 35 after rescuers recovered 30 bodies from the burned vessel. Search and identification work continue.
deck: Rescuers recovered 30 bodies after gaining access to the burned MV June Aster, raising the confirmed death toll to 35 as search and identification work continues off Coron, Palawan.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ferry Fire Off Coron Leaves at Least 5 Dead as Search Continues
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported at least five deaths while rescuers were still unable to fully enter the vessel, responders have recovered 30 additional bodies from inside the burned ferry, raising the confirmed death toll to 35.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Rescuers recovered 30 bodies from the burned passenger ferry MV June Aster on Friday, September 11, after responders were able to enter the vessel, raising the confirmed death toll from five to 35.

Reuters reported that firefighters and rescuers gained access after intense heat and smoke had previously prevented a full search of the vessel. Associated Press separately reported the death toll at 35 and said 43 people had survived while 54 remained missing at the time of its latest report.
The vessel caught fire on the evening of September 9 while nearing Coron, Palawan, after sailing from Manila. The cause of the fire has not been established.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's first report
paragraphs: FMB News first reported on September 10 that at least five people had died and that rescue and passenger-accounting figures were still changing while the vessel remained too hot and smoke-filled for a complete internal search.

The new development is the recovery of 30 additional bodies from inside the ferry after responders gained access. That raises the confirmed death toll to 35 and materially changes the scale of the disaster. The September 10 report remains intact as the historical first report.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The ferry's original manifest listed 117 passengers and 17 crew members. Authorities later determined that two people on the manifest had not actually boarded, underscoring why official survivor, fatality and missing-person totals have required repeated reconciliation.

Reuters reported 43 people rescued as of Friday morning. AP later reported 43 survivors and 54 people still missing. Because identification and passenger accounting remain active, FMB News is not deriving a final missing-person count beyond figures directly attributed to current official or wire-service reporting.
MARINA has said survivor accounts included reports of two successive explosions before the fire spread, but no verified official finding has established the cause or origin of the blaze.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The jump in confirmed fatalities makes the June Aster fire one of the country's most serious recent passenger-vessel disasters and intensifies scrutiny of shipboard fire safety, emergency evacuation, passenger manifests, vessel inspection and maritime regulation.

For families, the immediate priority is identification of the recovered victims and reconciliation of the passenger list. For regulators, the next phase will be determining how the fire began, whether safety systems and procedures functioned as required, and whether preventable failures contributed to the loss of life.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The final number and identities of the dead, survivors and people still missing have not yet been fully reconciled in the latest reporting reviewed by FMB News.
The cause and point of origin of the fire remain under investigation. Reports of explosions are survivor accounts cited by authorities and are not, by themselves, a final determination of cause.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for official identification of the recovered victims, a reconciled passenger and crew accounting, Philippine Coast Guard and MARINA findings on the fire's origin, and any regulatory or enforcement action involving the vessel or its operator.

sections.heading: Reader note
paragraphs: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

verificationNotes: The rise in the confirmed death toll to 35 is independently reported by Reuters and Associated Press, both citing Philippine authorities or Coast Guard information.
Reuters reported that 30 bodies were recovered after responders gained access to the burned vessel; AP independently reported the resulting death toll of 35.
The article does not present survivor reports of explosions as a verified cause of the fire. The cause remains under investigation.
The article avoids deriving a final missing-person count because official passenger accounting and identification remain active and have changed during the response.
This is a material continuation of FMB News' September 10 first report. The visible Continues from link points to that earliest FMB News ferry-fire report, which remains unchanged.
